proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: pulling the cube identity back along x -> (x, x, -x) gives L^3 (x) [-1]^*L = [2]^*L, the case n = 2; the induction step pulls the cube identity back along x -> (x, x, [n-1]x), giving [n+1]^*L (x) L^2 (x) [n-1]^*L = [2]^*L (x) [n]^*L (x) [n]^*L; substituting the induction hypotheses for [2], [n], [n-1] and cancelling in the group of invertible modules yields the exponent identity for [n+1] (source lines 1957-1983)
